chunks: And from Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani who said: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Khaythama narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, from Jabir ibn Samra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
This Umma will remain with its affairs upright and prevailing over its enemy until twelve Caliphs have passed away from it.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of Caliphs in the Umma?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani in *Kitab al-Ghayba*, establishes the number twelve as a definitive marker for the continuity of legitimate leadership, a concept central to both Sunni and Shia eschatology. In Shia scholarship, it is specifically interpreted as referring to the Twelve Imams, linking the political stability of the early community to the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt. The narration underscores the divine promise that the Ummah remains 'upright' and victorious as long as this specific lineage of twelve leaders guides them.
